clue.text: Right integral to turmoil affecting leadership of six countries here?

definitions.text: Right integral to turmoil affecting leadership of six countries here?

indicators.note: integral to means forming a part within, so the letter for right sits inside the string of initials

parts.note: the leading letters of the six countries named in this puzzle's clues: Libya, Iran, Bahrain, Egypt, Tunisia, Yemen

explanation.surface: A question about what is at stake as upheaval sweeps the rulers of six nations in the Arab Spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here?' points to the grid itself: Libya, Iran, Bahrain, Egypt, Tunisia and Yemen all appear in other clues, and their initials L, I, B, E, T, Y take R between E and T. The whole clue also describes what the uprisings sought.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom from tyranny was the prize sought by protesters during the uprisings against those regimes.

clue.text: Puts up with recession being dealt with in a top-down way

indicators.text: being dealt with in a top-down way
indicators.note: in this down entry the top letter of the word is sent down to the bottom

parts.note: a slump is an economic recession

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates an economic downturn handled by managers from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top-down' sounds like management jargon; it means the first letter of SLUMP moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To lump it is an idiom for accepting something unpleasant without complaint.

clue.text: Bahrain government in trouble, world body taking interest finally in what goes on in souk?

indicators.note: a country in trouble is in disarray, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a world body

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of interest

explanation.surface: With Bahrain's regime in crisis, the United Nations takes an interest in the affairs of the marketplace.
explanation.walkthrough: A souk is an Arab market where haggling for a good deal is routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopping around for cheap deals is what a market haggler does.

clue.text: Movement in Iran gives way under pressure — but there are signs of a brighter future

indicators.note: movement in the letters of the country shifts them into a new order

parts.note: something that bows bends or yields when pressed

explanation.surface: A political movement in Iran collapses under pressure, yet there is hope ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcs of colour after a storm are traditional symbols of hope and better times.

clue.text: Until now, one's not proven to exist

definitions.text: Until now, one's not proven to exist

parts.note: yet means up to this time, as in 'not done yet'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something, so far, has not been shown to be real.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan abominable snowman is a creature whose existence remains unproven.

clue.text: US cargo transported in Pumas

indicators.note: transported suggests the cargo being shifted about, so its letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An American shipment is carried inside Puma cars or crates.
explanation.definitionFit: Puma and cougar are two names for the same big American cat, here in the plural.

clue.text: Originally Roman section of southern district in French city

indicators.note: in places the southern district inside the name of the French city

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy, France
an area is a district

explanation.surface: A guide to a quarter of a French city that was first built by the Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Caesarean section is traditionally said to be named after Julius Caesar's birth, hence 'Originally Roman'.
explanation.definitionFit: The surgical birth delivery is popularly linked to Julius Caesar, a Roman, giving the operation its name.

clue.text: Women can't stand going there

parts.note: reads as women disliking somewhere, but literally means women cannot use it standing up: a gents' fixture

explanation.definitionFit: A wall-mounted fixture in men's toilets is used standing, so women are excluded by anatomy.

clue.text: Perhaps a bowl of hummus with poultry's no-go, containing fat

parts.note: hummus is served as a dip, so 'Perhaps' marks it as one example

indicators.note: no in front of 'go' means those two letters are left out

parts.note: a goose is a farmyard bird, i.e. poultry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hummus with chicken is banned at a dinner, being too fatty.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fatty tissue, so the word describes things holding fat.

clue.text: Change to Tunisia's state

indicators.note: change applied to the letters means rearranging them into something new

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Regime change comes to Tunisia during the Arab Spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a state of affairs, the condition things are in.

clue.text: Revolutionary form of existentialism, rejecting originator and embracing our own ends

indicators.note: a form of a word can be a reshaping of its letters, so these letters are rearranged
the originator is the first letter, which is rejected, i.e. dropped from the long word
the ends of 'our' and 'own' are their final letters

explanation.surface: A philosopher's school is remodelled, disowning its founder and adopting some of our own ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting originator' drops the opening E of existentialism; 'embracing' adds R and N, the 'ends' of 'our own'; 'form of' then rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Marx and Lenin's communist doctrine is a political revolutionary by creed.

clue.text: Dirty books discovered in carriage

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it, so the books sit within the carriage

parts.note: a shay is a light horse-drawn carriage (a chaise)
B is an abbreviation for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: Smutty literature is found hidden away in a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby clothes or rooms are worn and grubby, much like something dirty.

clue.text: Fear a Hebridean hip-hop comeback?

indicators.note: a comeback here means the whole string of pieces is read coming back, from the end

parts.note: Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
rap is a style of hip-hop music

explanation.surface: Someone worries about a Scottish island rap artist staging a return.
explanation.definitionFit: An irrational, persistent suspicion that others mean harm is a kind of fear.

clue.text: Puts the squeeze on smooth West Indies before game is cut short

parts.note: to sand wood is to make it smooth
WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies, the Caribbean cricket team

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the game's name is lopped off

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the West Indies are ironed out before rain shortens the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To sandwich something is to press it tightly between two others, squeezing it in.

clue.text: It's time Libya shifted balance

indicators.note: shifted means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Time for Libya to change, upsetting the regional balance of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Stability means steadiness or equilibrium, a state of being in balance.

clue.text: Putting bed on north side of yard encouraged embryonic leaf

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: in a down entry the north side is the top, so the first letter of yard is taken

parts.note: to lead someone on is to encourage them

explanation.surface: A gardener puts a flower bed by the north wall of the yard to encourage young growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed leaf is the first leaf formed in the embryo of a seed plant.

clue.text: Stupid Boy's cycling cap

indicators.note: cycling means letters are moved round from the front of the word to the back

parts.note: Private Pike in the BBC sitcom Dad's Army is called 'stupid boy' by Captain Mainwaring

explanation.surface: A foolish lad's bicycling helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a long-running British TV comedy about the Home Guard; 'cycling' moves PI from the front of PIKE to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A French military cap with a flat circular top and a peak is a kepi.

clue.text: Egypt minister thrown out in vacation

indicators.note: thrown out means scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An Egyptian government minister is expelled while on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacation in its literal sense means clearing out, vacating, a space or building.

clue.text: A wealthy investor's principally going to be shrewd

indicators.note: going means departing, so a letter leaves the word for wealthy

parts.note: wealthy means rich

indicators.note: principally means at its head, so the first letter of investor's is taken

explanation.surface: A rich backer is chiefly heading for being clever with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch can mean cunning or knowing, as in an arch smile from a sly person.

clue.text: Conservative splitter -and another

parts.note: one who splits from a group or party is a leaver

explanation.surface: A Tory defects from the party, and a second follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative splitter' builds the word, and 'and another' says the whole is a second kind of splitter: a butcher's chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy chopper that splits meat is another thing that divides, alongside a defector.

clue.text: Same, not different progeny for one producing a chip off the old block?

definitions.text: one producing a chip off the old block?

indicators.note: different signals that the letters of 'Same' and 'not' are made into something else

parts.note: a son is progeny, an example of offspring

explanation.surface: A child described as not like a parent, despite the saying that he is a chip off the old block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chip off the old block' usually means a child like a parent; here it is a literal chip of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason who cuts building stone literally produces chips off blocks.

clue.text: Fish-what's turned up as raw material for soap

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tuna is a fish
eh is an exclamation meaning what?, with 's added

explanation.surface: A puzzled shout about a fish that turned up as an ingredient for soap.
explanation.definitionFit: The fatty kernel of an African tree yields a butter used in soaps and cosmetics.

clue.text: Foil for Reeves and Minchin

parts.note: Vic Reeves is a British comedian
Tim Minchin is an Australian comedian and musician

explanation.surface: A straight man is needed for two comedians.
explanation.walkthrough: Vic Reeves is an English comic known for surreal TV shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A foil is someone who serves as a butt or target for others, like a dupe.

clue.text: Lie in bed, tossing and turning after such food?

definitions.text: Lie in bed, tossing and turning after such food?

indicators.note: restless tossing and turning suggests the letters of the phrase being thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lies awake restlessly after eating something that disagreed with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Food unfit to eat is the kind likely to keep you up at night with a bad stomach.

clue.text: Goddess explaining how to begin aerobics?

indicators.note: to begin points at the opening of the word aerobics, its first letters spelt out in order

parts.note: the explanation of the order is 'then', linking the first letter to the next one
the explanation of the order is 'then', linking the first letter to the next one

explanation.surface: A fitness deity explains the right way to start an exercise class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how to begin aerobics' is spelling, not exercise: the word starts A, then E, so the second letter E follows the explaining word THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war.

clue.text: Opponent of reform in Yemen

indicators.note: reform in the country's name means remaking its letters in a new form

explanation.surface: The foe of political reform in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is a foe or adversary, someone against you.

clue.text: See 2
A divine duet — nice arrangement, select crowd

indicators.note: a musical arrangement of the duet reworks it, so its letters with those of 'nice' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavenly duet in a pleasing arrangement for a choice gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience admitted only by invitation is a selected crowd.

clue.text: Farm employee reversing cart succeeds, not taking ages

indicators.note: a reversing vehicle goes backwards, so the word for cart is read from the end

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

indicators.note: not taking means leaving out the letters of 'ages'

parts.note: to succeed at something is to manage it, so succeeds is manages
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmhand backs up a cart successfully and quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardman works around a farmyard doing general labouring jobs.

clue.text: Idiot twisting with passion has nothing to lose in "Strictly"

indicators.note: twisting round means the word for idiot is turned to read backwards

parts.note: git is British slang for an idiot

indicators.note: to lose means to drop a letter from the phrase for with passion

parts.note: to do something hotly is to do it with passion
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A fool dancing with fervour has little chance in the TV show Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: "Strictly" suggests the BBC dance contest Strictly Come Dancing, but it is the plain adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold firmly or control rigidly is to do so in a close, rigorous way.
